solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Notice doctor cuddling new arrival

parts.note: AD is short for advertisement, a notice

indicators.note: to cuddle is to wrap round, so the vet's letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor hugs a newborn as the birth is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New arrival' reads as a baby, but 'new' belongs to the wordplay and only 'arrival' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means a coming or appearance, the arrival of something notable.

clue.text: In military, captain's first — plus handsome escort

indicators.note: in places the other letters inside the army word

parts.note: the army is the military

indicators.note: first means the opening letter only

parts.note: first letter C
and means plus

explanation.surface: An army captain has a good-looking companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Arm candy is slang for an attractive companion taken to events mainly to be shown off.

clue.text: Prophetic RC HQ ejects a nun finally

indicators.note: ejects means throws out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: the Vatican is the headquarters of the Roman Catholic Church

indicators.note: finally means the last letter

parts.note: last letter N

explanation.surface: The Catholic headquarters throws out a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: Vatic is a literary word for oracular, foretelling the future like a seer.

clue.text: PIN's missing a zero

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a nail is a metal pin

explanation.surface: A bank card's PIN lacks a zero digit.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised, PIN looks like a personal identification number; it is a plain pin, a nail.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil means nothing, the score of zero in sport.

clue.text: Distort way fighter appears

parts.note: to warp is to twist out of shape
a lane is a narrow way or road

explanation.surface: A twisted road reveals a fighter jet coming into view.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter is a combat aircraft, a type of military plane.

clue.text: After a week minor perhaps gets bolshie

indicators.note: after puts the minor piece later, following the other letters

parts.note: a ward is a minor under a guardian's care

explanation.surface: After a week, a youngster becomes rebellious.
explanation.walkthrough: A ward of court is a child placed under legal guardianship. Bolshie is British slang for uncooperative.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie means difficult and uncooperative, and awkward also means hard to deal with.

clue.text: Favourite staff all got up in gold, ready for OPEC?

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
a rod is a staff or stick

indicators.note: in puts the reversed word inside the gold letters

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: got up means raised, which in a down clue reads the word backwards

explanation.surface: A favourite's staff all dressed up in gold, fit for an oil cartel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is slang for cash; OPEC, the oil exporters' cartel, earns its money in dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: A petrodollar is a US dollar earned by oil-exporting countries, money that oil states hold.

clue.text: Obsessive is, say, pointing up a source of relief

parts.note: anal is slang for obsessively fussy

indicators.note: pointing up in a down clue means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: EG (for example) means say

explanation.surface: An obsessive person points out where relief comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'pointing up' reads IS and EG from the bottom upwards, making GESI.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the loss of pain, the painkilling effect that brings comfort to a sufferer.

clue.text: Speech lauding record year under Brussels

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts these letters below the Brussels letters

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union, EU
a log is a record

explanation.surface: A speech praising a record year under EU rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is an address praising someone, often given at a funeral.

clue.text: Spirit bottle regularly found in enclosure

indicators.note: found in means placed inside the enclosure word

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter

parts.note: alternate letters OTE

explanation.surface: A bottle of spirits is regularly found in an animal pen.
explanation.walkthrough: Poteen is illicitly distilled Irish whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Poteen is an Irish distilled liquor, so it is a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Mike and others argue about face of kroner that could be forged

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
et al is Latin shorthand for and others

indicators.note: about here signals turning the word round, read backwards

parts.note: to row is to argue

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, its opening letter

parts.note: first letter K

explanation.surface: Mike and colleagues dispute whether a Scandinavian coin could be counterfeit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forged' suggests counterfeit money, but metal is forged by a smith in a forge.
explanation.definitionFit: Metalwork is articles made of metal, shaped by hammering in a forge.

clue.text: Track dog crossing river

indicators.note: crossing here means spanning, so the dog verb's letters lie across the other piece

parts.note: to tail someone is to dog them, follow closely
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tracker dog follows a scent across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path or the marks left behind, so it is a track in both senses.

clue.text: Token beer knocked back in old ship in Orkney, say

indicators.note: in places the token and drink inside the ship's name

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek legend
a chip is a gambling token

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, so the beer word is read backwards

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone drinks a beer bought with a token aboard an old vessel moored in the Orkneys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking the beer, but it reverses it. Orkney is a group of islands off northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Orkney is a chain of many islands, an example of an island group.

clue.text: Secure cheeky child the Spanish firework upset

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a banger is a loud firework

explanation.surface: A cheeky child tips over a Spanish firework.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger, in Britain, is a firework that explodes with a loud bang.
explanation.definitionFit: Impregnable means unable to be captured or broken into, so safe from attack.

clue.text: Crack band with no name

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a gang is a band of people

explanation.surface: An elite crack band performs without its name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack band' suggests an expert group, but 'Crack' alone is the definition, a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a wisecrack, a quip, which is the same as a joke.

clue.text: Cast stand up for rubbish collector

indicators.note: to cast metal is to mould it into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An actor's cast rises to its feet for a binman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish collector' suggests a binman, but it is the household gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan is the flat scoop into which sweepings and dirt are brushed.

clue.text: Finish off looking round classy creature on bed

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shortened word goes round the other letter
finish off means remove the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: searching is looking
U means upper-class, classy

explanation.surface: Someone stops searching around a posh creature in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' sounds like a bedroom, but this is the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea urchin is a spiny marine animal living on the ocean floor.

clue.text: Doctor works with unknown fluid problem

parts.note: opus means a work, plural opera, but ops is the crossword abbreviation for works
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A doctor deals with a mystery case of fluid retention.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is the old name for oedema, a build-up of watery liquid in the body's tissues.

clue.text: Overdraft in wobbly organisation's a setback

indicators.note: in puts those letters inside the rearranged word
organisation means arranging, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: OD is the bank abbreviation for overdrawn or overdraft

explanation.surface: Going overdrawn in a shaky company is a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' looks like a company, but it is the anagram signal for 'wobbly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A body blow is a severe disappointment, a figurative heavy punch to the torso.

clue.text: Northern swimmer Jack sent round extract from Moby-Dick?

indicators.note: sent round means turned back, so the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: an eel is a swimming fish
AB (able seaman) is a sailor, as is a jack

explanation.surface: A sailor in the north reads a passage from Melville's whaling novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract' looks like a quotation from the book, but it is something extracted from a whale, Moby-Dick being one.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleen, or whalebone, comes from the mouths of filter-feeding whales, so it could be taken from the famous whale.

clue.text: Converted cardinal hosts society correspondent

indicators.note: hosts means contains, so the cardinal's name holds the other letter

parts.note: John Henry Newman converted from Anglicanism to Catholicism and became a cardinal

explanation.surface: A cardinal who converted entertains a society reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsman is a journalist, and a correspondent is a reporter for a paper.

clue.text: New rock producer's refreshing vocal number

indicators.note: refreshing means making anew, so these letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A new rock band's producer revamps a vocal track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New rock producer' suggests a music producer, but it is a geological one.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano erupts lava that cools into freshly formed igneous stone.

clue.text: The sixth queen raised capital

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral six

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, reversing the name

parts.note: Anne was a queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: The sixth queen is crowned with capital riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria.

clue.text: Malagasy native's refurbished centre

indicators.note: refurbished means done up anew, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A man from Madagascar has a renovated centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Malagasy native' reads as a person but is an animal of Madagascar.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenrec is a small insect-eating mammal found in Madagascar.

clue.text: Organ needing repairs every so often

indicators.note: every so often means at regular intervals, so take every second letter

explanation.surface: A church organ needs occasional maintenance.
explanation.walkthrough: The organ is a church instrument on the surface, but a body part in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is the body part used for hearing, one of the body's organs.

clue.text: Marshal Ney was ready for the first item in his diary?

definitions.text: the first item in his diary

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Napoleon's Marshal Ney was prepared for the first engagement in his calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals, so 'Marshal' looks like his title, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: January the first opens the calendar year, so it is the earliest date listed in any diary.

clue.text: Autocrat has to abandon singular repository

indicators.note: to abandon means to leave out, so that letter goes

parts.note: a despot is an autocrat
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A dictator must give up a single storehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse or warehouse where goods are kept.

clue.text: Bloke in pub, backsliding — after this treatment?

indicators.note: backsliding means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
in puts the bloke inside the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
he is a male, a bloke

explanation.surface: A man relapses in the pub, needing treatment afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backsliding' suits a relapsing drinker but is the reversal signal; 'after this' points to the drinking that leads to the treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is short for rehabilitation, a course of therapy for addiction.

clue.text: German city contracted one mate working for it?

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: Munich is a city in Bavaria
I is the Roman numeral for one
a pal is a mate

explanation.surface: A worker contracted to a German city hires a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' refers back to the city: municipal staff work for a town or city.
explanation.definitionFit: Municipal describes the local council and its services, run on behalf of a town.

clue.text: I'm surprised there are no tips on exclusive

indicators.note: no tips means both end letters are cut off

parts.note: a scoop is an exclusive news story

explanation.surface: Astonishment that a newspaper exclusive has no leads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coo!' is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Coo is an exclamation expressing astonishment, like 'well I never'.

clue.text: Is US aviation pioneer able to abandon British watersport?

parts.note: can means be able to

indicators.note: to abandon means to leave behind, so that letter goes

parts.note: William Boeing founded the American aircraft company

explanation.surface: A question whether an American flier could give up a British water sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Canoeing is paddling a light boat, a recreational activity on rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Grovel, offering punch and whiskey to wife

parts.note: a KO is a knockout punch
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone grovels, offering a punch and a whiskey to their wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To kowtow is to kneel and bow deeply, behaving with abject servility.
